title: A free baseline removes all 30 added four-second recovery-cap exclusions in 607 selected Allen curves
abstract: We tested whether a constant baseline changes a prior slow-recovery constraint in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1. The primary sample had 607 selected mouse VisP and human TCx connections with four pause summaries and at least five trials per pause. At an assumed change limit of 0.10 normalized units, a same-sign positive exponential mixture with a four-second time cap and zero baseline had 513 failures. A free constant baseline reduced this count to 395. All 30 exclusions added by the cap relative to the uncapped zero-baseline model became compatible. The same result held for all 50 and five cap-added cases in the overlapping three-trial and ten-trial selections. Bounded grid linear programs resolved all tested capped threshold cases. The result shows dependence on the zero-baseline assumption. It does not show a measured baseline error or exclude slow biological modes. Separate protocol trials, assumed error limits, selected slices and sparse human data limit inference. Code, proof, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are excluded.

display.caption: A free constant baseline reduces failures of a four-second recovery-cap model. Counts describe selected curves at an assumed 0.10 normalized change limit.
